sentences.text: Hauffiosaurus zanoni was a medium-sized plesiosaur measuring approximately 3.4 meters in length.
The skull of Hauffiosaurus zanoni measures about 430 mm along the midline.
The holotype specimen of Hauffiosaurus tomistomimus measures 4.83 meters in length.
The individual belonging to the holotype of Hauffiosaurus longirostris is estimated to have measured approximately 4.83 meters in total body length.
The genus Hauffiosaurus was first named by Frank Robin O'Keefe in 2001, with Hauffiosaurus zanoni designated as the type species.
Two additional species, H. longirostris and H. tomistomimus, were assigned to the genus Hauffiosaurus in 2011.
The teeth of Hauffiosaurus were slender, elongated, and possessed fine longitudinal ridges.
The combination of slender, ridged teeth and a long rostrum in Hauffiosaurus was effective for piercing soft prey.
Smith & Dyke (2008) were the first to identify Hauffiosaurus as a basal pliosauroid.
Hauffiosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic (early Toarcian stage) and is known from fossil sites in Holzmaden, Germany, and Yorkshire, United Kingdom.
Hauffiosaurus lived from 184.2 to 174.7 million years ago during the Toarcian stage.
